subject: Clarifying privacy roles and PII handling after Tuesday demo
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Porter <olivia@mediinfo.com>, David Li <david.li@mediinfo.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Oct 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: quick recap + next steps on privacy questions

Hi Olivia / David —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the key privacy/data-handling items you asked us to clarify and propose next steps so we can keep the procurement thread moving: 

1) Controller vs Processor: MediInfo would be controller for patient data you supply; Redwood operates as processor for API calls unless otherwise contractually assigned. We are happy to map textbook responsibilities in the DPA and accommodate limited controller obligations if needed (e.g., no marketing use).

2) Subprocessors: You asked for a list and a chance to veto any run-time subprocessors for this pilot. We maintain a vetted subprocessors registry; we can provide the register and support a 30-day notice/veto for any new subprocessors that would access your production data.

3) Breach notification timing: Our standard DPA provides 72-hour notification for confirmed incidents. We heard you prefer 48 hours for security incidents affecting PII — we flagged that as an ask for Legal.

4) Data residency & logs: The pilot will target us-east region for now; we can route all inference and logs to your dedicated VPC (Redwood Private) if you require. Retention windows (logs + debug traces) default to 90 days; you asked about a 180-day option and export capabilities.

5) PII handling & retention: We observed your ask to delete records on request and to retain minimal logs for troubleshooting. We can scope a retention policy and confirm delete flows (API delete + background purge).

Immediate next steps I propose: 
- I will loop in Marissa (Legal) and Nikhil (SE) to provide the redlined DPA and a simple dataflow diagram (attachments coming).
- Please confirm which of the three items (subprocessor vetos / 48-hour breach window / 180-day logs) are deal-breakers vs negotiable for procurement.
- If useful, we can schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call Thurs 10/4.

Thanks — I’ll attach the redline and a high-level dataflow in my next note.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147

Attachment: (will follow)

From: Olivia Porter <olivia@mediinfo.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Li <david.li@mediinfo.com>, Aaron Chen <aaron.chen@mediinfo.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Oct 2028 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick recap + next steps on privacy questions

Hi Sean —

Appreciate the recap — that aligns with our notes. A few clarifying questions before we loop Legal: 

- Subprocessor registry: can you provide current list (including cloud infra and telemetry vendors) and confirm whether any subprocessors currently have access to unredacted inference payloads?
- Breach notification: 48 hours is our preference for incidents impacting PII; 72 is often a blocker for our InfoSec team. Is 48 hours something Redwood can commit to contractually for this pilot?
- Data residency: For PHI-containing payloads we need logs and inference to remain within our US-only account and to prevent any egress to multi-region telemetry services. Can Redwood point to a concrete config for that?

If you can send the DPA redline + a dataflow map, I’ll route to David and Aaron (Legal/Procurement). Depending on the redlines, we may ask for a short legal call.

Thanks,
Olivia Porter
Head of Product Integrations | MediInfo Health
olivia@mediinfo.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Porter <olivia@mediinfo.com>, David Li <david.li@mediinfo.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick recap + next steps on privacy questions

Hi Olivia + team —

Thanks for the clear list. I’m Redwood Legal; copying Nikhil to handle the infra/config details. Quick answers below and I attached the redline for your review.

1) Subprocessors: Attached redline includes our current subprocessors (GCP: compute & storage, S3 mirrors for backup, telemetry vendor "Observr") and notes that only our compute layer holds unredacted inference payloads for processing. Observability traces are pseudonymized by default, and we can provide a separate export pipeline that strips payloads. If you’d like, we can provide a signed NDA + technical access for a narrow audit of the registry.

2) Breach notification: Our standard is 72 hours for confirmed incidents. We understand 48 hours is preferable for MediInfo. We can propose a 48-hour notification clause for incidents where PII/PHI is reasonably likely to have been accessed, with caveats around investigation time and customer notification coordination. Please note we cannot commit to 48 hours for every suspected incident without preliminary triage. Language proposed in attached redline (see §5.2).

3) Data residency & logs: Nikhil — can you confirm the steps to ensure inference + logs remain in the US VPC and how we would disable telemetry egress?

4) Retention & deletes: The redline introduces a configurable retention window (90 / 180 / custom) and an API-driven delete + background purge workflow. We recommend recording the chosen window in the SOW.

Next steps I suggest: 
- Please review the attached redline (Redwood_PrivacyAddendum_Redline_v1.pdf).
- Nikhil will reply with a short technical note and the dataflow PNG showing where logs live and how payloads are protected.
- If the 48-hour breach notification is non-negotiable, we should set up a 30-minute legal sync. Otherwise we can iterate in-markup.

Attachments: Redwood_PrivacyAddendum_Redline_v1.pdf; SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2027.pdf; dataflow_medinfo_v1.png

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Porter <olivia@mediinfo.com>, David Li <david.li@mediinfo.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick recap + next steps on privacy questions

Hi Olivia / David —

Quick technical note on residency and telemetry: 

- For the pilot we will deploy a tenant-scoped Redwood Private instance in your AWS account (us-east-1). Inference compute + KV caches remain in your VPC subnets.
- Logs: application logs and token-level traces are written to an S3 bucket in your account by default. We provide two telemetry modes: (1) minimal metrics only (no payloads), or (2) full traces with payload redaction. We will default to minimal metrics unless you opt in.
- Subprocessors: Observr is used for aggregated metrics only and does not receive payloads by default; we can disable Observr telemetry egress for your tenant.
- Breach detection & notification: Our monitoring rules generate an internal investigation ticket immediately. For confirmed breaches affecting PII/PHI we will escalate to Marissa and commit to the 48-hour notification language as proposed in the redline with the investigatory caveat called out.

If that aligns, Sean — I’ll prepare a short runbook and include the dataflow PNG we discussed (attached in Marissa’s message). Happy to jump on a 20-minute technical call with your infra/InfoSec folks.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai
